Learned counsel for the petitioner files a memo, seeking leave of the Court to withdraw the writ petition, which reads as under:
NC: 2024:KHC-K:8430 "MEMO FOR WITHDRAWAL OF THE W.P.
The Petitioner is Respondent No.2 in M.V.C. No.117/2018 filed by the Respondent No.1 herein for compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for an accident occurred on 23/02/2016.

The Tribunal awarded Rs.9,14,500/- with interest and costs holding that the Writ Petitioner liable to pay in the first instance and recover from the Respondent No.2 herein who is the owner of the insured Auto as there was no valid DL.

The Respondent No.2/insurer is the Petitioner herein filed an application under section 51 of the CPC praying the Court not to disburse the amount till the Owner of the vehicle furnishes security in view of the Apex Court Judgment in Challa Bharatamma's case.

The Tribunal rejected the Petition as per the Order dated The United India Insurance Company ... vs Basangouda @ Basavaraj And Ors on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193122704/
2 22/12/2023 which is challenged.

without considering contention of the petitioner, has passed the impugned order.
It is learnt that the Respondent No.1 got the amount released.
The W.P has become infructuous.
Hence, this Memo is filed for withdrawal of the above Writ Petition.
The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to dismiss the above W.P. in the interest of justice and equity."
The memo is placed on record.
3. The writ petition is dismissed as withdrawn.

Sd/-
(S.R.KRISHNA KUMAR) JUDGE LG
